task: This is a synthetic writing exercise. Using these fictional reporting notes, write a newspaper news story for general readers. Draw only on the supplied notes; do not invent additional reported events, scenes, or quotations. Write from this reporting snapshot as of November 3, 2024. Include a headline. Target 450 to 650 words. Follow AP style.

facts.text: The Harrington Bay Storm Surge Barrier closed on October 31, 2024, for its first operational activation against Hurricane Vera, which made landfall at Category 2 strength with peak storm surge levels recorded at 3.1 meters.
The barrier held and the protected estuary area recorded surge levels of 0.4 meters, compared to 3.1 meters in unprotected reference areas to the north.
No flooding was reported within the barrier's protection zone, an area of 62 square kilometers including 38,000 residents and $14 billion in assessed property.

Benjamin Clarke, director of the Harrington Bay Coastal Authority, said: "The barrier performed exactly as modeled. We can now say with confidence that it will protect the city in storms of this category."
Chief engineer Dr. Ingrid Larsen said the 30 surge gates reached full closure in 84 minutes after the decision to activate, within the design specification of 90 minutes.
Flooding was reported at several points north of the barrier boundary during the storm; those areas are outside the protected zone.
The barrier took 11 years to plan and construct at a cost of $4.8 billion; it opened in March 2024.

Marine ecologist Dr. Simon Ward of Harrington University said the barrier's closure for the 18-hour storm duration temporarily blocked juvenile fish passage in the estuary; the ecological effect is under post-storm monitoring.
The barrier is designed to provide protection against storms up to Category 3 strength and surge events with a one-in-100-year probability.
Dr. Larsen said the closure used 14 of the 30 gates fully and the remaining 16 at 75% closure; the partial closure approach was designed to minimize flow disruption while maintaining protection.
Hurricane Vera produced 148 millimeters of rainfall over the Harrington watershed in six hours; stormwater drainage systems within the barrier zone operated without significant backup.

The authority said a full post-activation engineering inspection of all gate mechanisms will be completed before the next activation, which could occur at any point in the remaining Atlantic hurricane season.
Two other major coastal barrier projects in the eastern United States are under construction; neither has yet been operationally tested by a storm.
Storm surge caused 11 of the 14 deaths attributed to Hurricane Vera in the Harrington Bay region; all 11 occurred north of the barrier boundary.
Dr. Ward said the long-term ecological question is whether repeated barrier closures over the facility's design life of 50 years will alter the estuary's salinity gradients and sediment dynamics.
Clarke said the authority will conduct a lessons-learned review and publish its findings before the 2025 hurricane season.
The barrier's gates are maintained in a normally open position to allow tidal exchange; closure is triggered only when surge forecasts exceed a defined threshold.
A cost-benefit analysis commissioned by the authority in 2021 estimated the barrier would prevent $1.2 billion in storm damage annually under median hurricane frequency projections.
The Harrington Bay area experienced $6.8 billion in flood damage from Hurricane Petra in 2017, a storm of comparable surge intensity.
Larsen said two gate hydraulic actuators showed minor wear that will be addressed during the post-storm inspection but did not affect gate performance.
